stem: Japanese encephalitis vaccination is specifically recommended for which group in Australia?

options.text: Residents of the outer Torres Strait Islands
All Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people nationally
Preterm infants born in northern Queensland
Children attending childcare in northern Australia

explanation: Residents of the outer Torres Strait Islands are the correct group because Japanese encephalitis vaccination is targeted to specific high-risk geographic areas rather than recommended nationally for all children.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because residents of the outer Torres Strait Islands live in a recognised high-risk area where Japanese encephalitis vaccination is specifically recommended.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because the vaccine is not recommended for all Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people nationally; it is based on geographic risk.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because occupation alone does not determine this recommendation; residence in an affected area is the key factor.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because prematurity is not the indication for this vaccine; location-based risk is the relevant criterion.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because childcare attendance is not the specific indication for Japanese encephalitis vaccination; living in a high-risk area is.

source.hint: The disease is rarely seen on the Australian mainland, focusing the vaccine requirement on specific islands.
